investigation.thought: No evidence yet, so start with an unfiltered metric query that ranks every service and metric by deviation from baseline.

Metrics (E1) already point at currencyservice: a huge diskio jump plus a sharp latency rise. A second, independent telemetry kind is needed, so I'll check traces for currencyservice's own and caller-observed latency.

Metrics (E1) and traces (E2) independently point at currencyservice: its disk I/O deviation dwarfs every other signal, and callers see a 7.71x latency jump, so the evidence is enough to finish as a disk fault.

alternatives_rejected.why: Its latency-90 deviation (z=18.16, 90.8%) is much smaller than currencyservice's latency-50 (z=171.75, 858.7%), and it has no resource anomaly, so it reads as a downstream victim of currencyservice (E1). Checkout calls currency, and E2 shows callers of currencyservice slowing 7.71x.

Frontend latency-50 rises only 196.5% (z=26.69) against currencyservice's 858.7%. The only large resource anomaly anywhere is currencyservice_diskio (E1). Inbound latency to currencyservice jumped 5.07->39.07ms (E2), which fits frontend slowing as a result rather than causing it.

proposed_fix.description: Find what is driving the abnormal disk I/O on currencyservice (runaway logging, temp files, a noisy neighbour on the node, or an injected I/O stress process). Throttle or stop it, or move the currencyservice pod to a healthy node. Then confirm diskio and the inbound p50 latency return to baseline (about 5ms).
